la:adj:artus.html:
artus (not arctus), a, um, adj.
v. arma
, prop.
fitted; hence,
Lit., close, strait, narrow, confined, short, brief: exierunt regionibus artis,: claustra,; so : nec tamen haec ita sunt arta et astricta, ut ea laxare nequeamus,: artioribus apud populum Romanum laqueis tenebitur,: nullum vinculum ad astringendam fidem jure jurando majores artius esse voluerunt,: compages,: nexus,: arto stipata theatro,pressed together in a contracted theatre,: toga,a narrow toga without folds, (cf. exigua toga, ): nimis arta convivia,i. e. with too many guests, who are therefore compelled to sit close together, et saep.—Hence, subst.: artum, i, n., a narrow place or passage: ventus cum confercit, franguntur in arto montes nimborum, Lachm.: multiplicatis in arto ordinibus,; so : nec desilies imitator in artum,nor, by imitating, leap into a close place,.—
Trop., strict, severe, scanty, brief, small: sponte suā cecidit sub leges artaque jura,subjected himself to the severity of the laws,: Additae leges artae et ideo superbae quasque etc.,: vincula amoris artissima,: artior somnus, a sounder or deeper sleep, : arti commeatus,; ; cf.: in arto commeatus,: artissimae tenebrae,very thick darkness, (for which, in class. Lat., densus, v. Bremi ad h. l., and cf. densus) al.—So, colligere in artum, to compress, abridge: quae (volumina) a me collecta in artum,.—Of hope, small, scanty: spes artior aquae manantis,: ne spem sibi ponat in arto, diminish hope, expectation,

: quia plus quam unum ex patriciis creari non licebat, artior petitio quattuor petentibus erat,i. e. was harder, had less ground of hope,; and of circumstances in life, etc., straitened, distressing, wretched, needy, indigent (so in and after the Aug. per. for the class. angustus): rebus in artis,: artas res nuntiaret,: tam artis afflictisque rebus,; so : fortuna artior expensis,: ne in arto res esset,.—Adv.: artē (not arcte), closely, close, fast, firmly.

Lit.: arte (manus) conliga,: boves arte ad stipites religare,: arte continere aliquid,: aciem arte statuere,: arte accubare,.—Comp.: calorem artius continere,: artius astringi,: signa artius conlocare,: artius ire,: artius pressiusque conflictari,.—Sup.: milites quam artissime ire jubet,: artissime plantas serere,.—
Trop.: arte contenteque aliquem habere,; : arte et graviter dormire,soundly,: arte appellare aliquem,briefly, by shortening his name,: artius adstringere rationem,: abstinentiam artissime constringere,.—
Transf.: arte diligere aliquem,strongly, deeply,; so also .

la:verb:arto.gloss: to draw or press close together, fit, compress, contract, tighten
senses: to draw or press close together, fit, compress, contract, tighten
la:verb:arto.html:
arto (not arcto), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
1. artus
,
to draw or press close together, to compress, contract (not found in Cic.).
Lit.: omnia conciliatu artari possunt, * : libros,; : vitis contineri debet vimine, non artari,: angustias eas artantibus insulis parvis, quae etc.,.—
Trop., to contract, straiten, limit, curtail: fortuna humana fingit artatque ut lubet, i. e. in angustias redigit, Lind.; : tempus,to limit, circumscribe,; : se,to limit one's self, to retrench, —
In gen., to finish, conclude, .—Hence, artātus, a, um, P. a., contracted into a small compass; hence, narrow, close; and of time, short: pontus,: tempus,.

la:adj:artifex.html:
artĭfex, fĭcis, m.
ars-facio
.
Subst.
One that is master in the liberal arts (while opifex is a master in the artes sordidae; cf. ars, I. B. 1.), an artist, artificer: illi artifices corporis simulacra ignotis nota faciebant,: reponendarum (tegularum) nemo artifex (i. e. architectus) inire rationem potuit,: in armamentario multis talium operum (sc. tormentorum) artificibus de industriā inclusis,: ut aiunt in Graecis artificibus eos auloedos esse, qui citharoedi fieri non potuerint, sic, etc.,; cf. : artifices scaenici,; ; : artifex lignorum,a carpenter,; so, artifex lignarius,: artifices lapidum,masons,: artifex aerarius,a worker in bronze, (often thus used in Vulg. for opifex).—Also absol.: artifex,: multi artifices ex Graeciā venerunt,; so ; ; ; 41, 20; so ; ; et saep.—So of a charioteer, as in Gr. τεχνίτης: ne hoc gloriae artificis daretur (auriga standing just before),.—Of a physician, . —Of an orator or writer: Graeci dicendi artifices et doctores,: cum contra talem artificem (sc. Hortensium oratorem) dicturus essem,: politus scriptor atque artifex,. —
Trop., a master in any thing, in doing any thing, etc.: artifices ad corrumpendum judicium,: artifex callidus comparandarum voluptatum,: Cotta in ambitione artifex,: serendae in alios invidiae artifex, —
A maker, originator, author, contriver: si pulcher est hic mundus, si probus ejus artifex, etc.,: cujus (civitatis) artifex et conditor (est) Deus,: artifex omnium natura,: si indocta consuetudo tam est artifex suavitatis,: artificem (sc. malorum) mediis immittam Terea flammis,: vadit ad artificem dirae Polymestora caedis,: sceleris infandi artifex,.—Ironic.: O artificem probum!.—Also for a sly, cunning contriver, inventor of a thing (cf. ars, II. fin.): et mihi jam multi crudele canebant Artificis scelus,; . —
Adj.
Act., skilled in a thing; skilful, practised, ingenious, dexterous: Bomilcar et per homines talis negotii artifices itinera explorat,: miles decollandi artifex,: artifex faber de silvā,: tam artifices saltationis,.—Also of inanimate things: artifices Natura manus admovit,: Tellus artifices ne terat Osca manus,: artifex, ut ita dicam, stilus,: mobilitas ignea artifex ad formanda corpora,: vir tam artificis ingenii,—Poet. with inf.: venter, negatas artifex sequi voces,.—
Pass., skilfully prepared or made, artistic, artificial, ingenious: quattuor artifices vivida signa boves,: tantae tamque artifices argutiae,: artifex dimicatio,: motus,: manus libratur artifici temperamento,, 54, § 115: artifex vultus,: plaga,—Poet. of a horse, broken, trained, .

la:noun:artificium.gloss: art, craft, skill, talent, artifice, craftsmanship
senses: art, craft, skill, talent, artifice, craftsmanship
la:noun:artificium.html:
artĭfĭcĭum, ii, n.
artifex
.
In gen., the occupation of an artifex, a profession, trade, an employment, a handicraft, an art: Jam de artificiis et quaestibus, qui liberales habendi, qui sordidi sint, etc.,: ne opifices quidem tueri sua artificia possent, nisi, etc.,: in artificio perquam tenui et levi (sc. scaenico),: sordidum ancillareque,; so ; : de hoc artificio est nobis acquisitio, * : non tu in isto artificio accusatorio callidior es quam hic in suo,—
Esp.
Skill, knowledge, ingenuity in any thing: simulacrum Dianae singulari opere artificioque perfectum,; so : quae certis signis artificii notata sunt, Auct. ad .—
Theory, system (cf. ars, I. C. 1.): non esse eloquentiam ex artificio, sed artificium ex eloquentiā natum,: existimant artificium esse hoc quoddam non dissimile ceterorum, cujusmodi de ipso jure civili Crassus componi posse dicebat,: scientia cujusdam artificii non numquam dicitur prudentia, Auct. ad : artificium memoriae,mnemonics,.—
Skill serviceable in the attainment of any object, ingenuity, art, dexterity; and in a bad sense, craft, cunning, artifice (cf. ars, II.): id ipsum, quod contra me locutus es, artificio quodam es consecutus,: opus est non solum ingenio, verum etiam artificio quodam singulari,: vicinitas non assueta mendaciis, non fucosa, non fallax, non erudita artificio simulationis,: non virtute, neque in acie vicisse Romanos, sed artificio quodam et scientiā oppugnationis,: quorum artificiis effectum est, ut res publica in hunc statum perveniret, id. ap. , C. fin.

la:noun:artus.html:
artus, ūs, m.
id.
, mostly plur. (artua, n., ; quoted in .—Hence, dat. acc. to Vel. Long. p. 2229 P. and P. artibus; yet the ancient grammarians give their decision in favor of artubus, which form is also supported by the best MSS.; cf. arcus.—The singular is found only in ; , and P.).
Lit., a joint: molles commissurae et artus (digitorum),: suffraginum artus,: elapsi in pravum artus,: dolor artuum,gout,.—Sometimes connected with membra, : copia materiaï Cogitur interdum flecti per membra, per artus,in every joint and limb,; ; ; cf. Baumg.-Crus., Clavis ad Suet.: cernere laceros artus, truncata membra,.—
Trop., the muscular strength in the joints; hence, in gen., strength, power: Ἐπιχαρμεῖον illud teneto; nervos atque artus esse sapientiae, non temere credere,.—More freq.,
The limbs in gen. (very freq., esp. in the poets; in Lucr. about sixty times): cum tremulis anus attulit artubus lumen, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 36 Vahl.); so ; cf. ; : artubus omnibus contremiscam,: dum nati (sc. Absyrti) dissupatos artus captaret parens, vet. poet. ap. : copia concita per artus Omnīs,: moribundi artus,: rogumque parari Vidit et arsuros supremis ignibus artus, etc.,: salsusque per artus Sudor iit,; : veste strictā et singulos artus exprimente,and showing each limb,: artus in frusta concident,; ; ib. Job, 16, 8.—Of plants: stat per se vitis sine ullo pedamento, artus suos in se colligens,its tendrils,, where Jahn reads arcus.

la:noun:articulus.gloss: a point connecting various parts of the body; joint, knot, knuckle.
senses: a point connecting various parts of the body; joint, knot, knuckle.
a short clause; a single word; pronoun, pronominal adjective or article
a member, part, division, point, article
a point in time, moment; division of time, space
a positive decimal integer consisting of a non-zero digit multiplied by a positive integral power of ten.
la:noun:articulus.html:
artĭcŭlus, i, m.dim.
2. artus
,
a small member connecting various parts of the body, a joint, knot, knuckle.
Lit.: nodi corporum, qui vocantur articuli,: hominis digiti articulos habent ternos, pollex binos,: summus caudae articulus,: crura sine nodis articulisque,: ipso in articulo, quo jungitur capiti cervix,: auxerat articulos macies,i. e. had made more joints, had made the bones visible,: articulorum dolores habere,i. e. gouty pains,; cf. : postquam illi justa cheragra Contudit articulos, * ; cf. : gladiatorem vehementis impetus excipit adversarii mollis articulus,.—Hence, molli articulo tractare aliquem, to touch one gently, softly, .—Of plants: ineunte vere in iis (vitibus), quae relicta sunt, exsistit, tamquam ad articulos sarmentorum, ea quae gemma dicitur,; : ante quam seges in articulum eat,; so . —Of mountains, a hill connecting several larger mountains: montium articuli,.—
With an extension of the idea, a limb, member, in gen. (cf. 2. artus), * .—Hence also for a finger, ; so ; : quot manus atteruntur, ut unus niteat articulus!: ab eo missus est articulus manūs,: aspiciebat articulos manūs,: erexit me super articulos manuum mearum, on the fingers or palms of my hands, . —
Trop.
Of discourse, a member, part, division: articulus dicitur, cum singula verba intervallis distinguuntur caesā oratione, hoc modo: acrimoniā, voce, vultu adversarios perterruisti, Auct. ad : continuatio verborum soluta multo est aptior atque jucundior, si est articulis membrisque (κόμμασι καὶ κώλοις) distincta, quam si continuata ac producta, : (genus orationis) fluctuans et dissolutum eo quod sine nervis et articulis fluctuat huc et illuc, Auct. ad .— Hence,a short clause,; also,a single word,: articulus Est praesentis temporis demonstrationem continet,: hoc articulo Quisque omnes significantur,.—In gram. the pronn. hic and quis, Müll.; the article, .—
Of time.
A point of time, a moment: commoditatis omnes articulos scio,.—With tempus: qui hunc in summas angustias adductum putaret, ut eum suis conditionibus in ipso articulo temporis astringeret,at the most critical moment,: in ipsis quos dixi temporum articulis,: si de singulis articulis

temporum deliberabimus, August. ap. ; also without tempus: in ipso articulo,at the fit moment, at the nick of time,.—With dies: in articulo diei illius ingressus est,on that very day,.—And with res: in articulo rerum,; also in articulo, instantly, immediately, = statim, .—Hence with the idea extended,

A space, division of time: hi cardines singulis articulis dividuntur,: octo articuli lunae,: articulus austrinus, i. e. in which auster blows, .—
Of other abstract things, part, division, point: per eosdem articulos (i.e. per easdem honorum partes) et gradus producere, August. ap. : stationes in mediis latitudinum articulis, quae vocant ecliptica,; : ventum est ergo ad ipsum articulum causae, i. e. ventum ad rei cardinem,the turning-point,.

la:adj:artificiosus.gloss: full of skill, skilful, artful, ingenious
senses: full of skill, skilful, artful, ingenious
according to the rules of art
la:adj:artificiosus.html:
artĭfĭcĭōsus, a, um, adj.
artificium
.
Act., accomplished in art, skilful, artistic (perh. found only in Cic. and Auct. ad Her.): rhetores elegantissimi atque artificiosissimi,: quod si artificiosum est intellegere, quae sunt ex arte scripta, multo est artificiosius ipsum scribere ex arte, Auct. ad : ipsius mundi natura non artificiosa solum, sed plane artifex,: Zeno naturam ita definit, ut eam dicat ignem esse artificiosum ad gignendum progredientem viā,, § 57.—
Pass. (cf. artifex, II. B.), on which much art has been bestowed, made with art, artificial, ingenious: utraeque (sc. venae et arteriae) vim quandam incredibilem artificiosi operis divinique testantur,: Epicurus autem nec non volt, si possit, plane et aperte loqui: nec de re obscurā, ut physici; aut artificiosā, ut mathematici,.—
According to the rules of art, artificial (esp. freq. in opp. to naturalis, natural): ea genera divinandi non naturalia, sed artificiosa dicuntur,; so several times Auct. ad al. —Adv.: artĭfĭcĭōsē, in skilful manner, skilfully: digerere aliquid,: dicere aliquid,: ambulare,: commutare aliquid, Auct. ad .—Comp.: multo artificiosius efficere aliquid,.—Sup.: artificiosissime facere, Auct. ad .

la:verb:articulo.gloss: to divide into single members or joints
senses: to divide into single members or joints
la:verb:articulo.html:
artĭcŭlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
articulus
, lit.
to divide into single members or joints; used only trop. of discourse, to utter distinctly, to articulate: hasce voces mobilis articulat verborum daedala lingua,the nimble tongue articulates,: verba,: sonos,.—Hence, artĭcŭlātus, a, um, P.a., prop., furnished with joints; hence distinct: verba, Sol. c. 65: vox,, and in gram.: articulata (vox) est, quae coartata, hoc est copulata, cum aliquo sensu mentis ejus, qui loquitur, profertur, P.; so .—* Adv.: artĭcŭlātē, distinctly, articulately: loqui,.

la:adv:articulatim.html:
artĭcŭlātim, adv.
articulatus
.
Joint by joint, limb by limb, piecemeal: aliquem concidere,: membra (pueri) articulatim dividit, poët. ap. ; cf. Planck, Eur. Medea, p. 102: comminuere articulatim diem, Plaut. Fragm. ap. .—
Trop., of discourse, properly divided (v. articulus, II. A.); hence, clearly, distinctly, point by point: verba discernere articulatim, Lucr. 4, 555: aliquid explicare,: aliquid articulatim distincteque dicere, * .

la:adj:artificialis.html:
artĭfĭcĭālis, e, adj.
artificium
,
of or belonging to art, artificial, according to the rules of art (perh. only in Quint.): probationes,; so ; : ratio,.—Once subst.: artĭfĭ-cĭālia, ium, n., things conformable to the rules of art, .—Adv.: artĭ-fĭcĭālĭter, according to art (opp. inartificialiter): se gerere,.

la:noun:arteria.html:
artērĭa, ae, f. (artērĭum, i, n.,
v.infra), = ἀρτηρία.
The windpipe: arteria ad pulmonem atque cor pertinens,; ; so ; —From its internal roughness, also called arteria aspera (Gr. τραχεῖα ἀρτηρία): cum aspera arteria (sic enim a medicis appellatur) ostium habeat adjunctum linguae radicibus,; .—And since it consists of two parts, also in the plur.: laeduntur arteriae, Auct. ad : arteriae reticendo acquiescunt,; ; ; ; .—Once in the neutr. plur.: artērĭa, ōrum, * .—
An artery: sanguis per venas in omne corpus diffunditur et spiritus per arterias,; cf. fin.; ; arteriarum pulsus citatus aut tardus, etc.,: arteria incisa non coit neque sanescit,.—Sometimes it interchanges with vena; cf.
